body.p: Status of the Application

By this Amendment, Claims 1, 6, and 7 have been amended for clarity. No new subject matter has been added. Claims 2 and 5 have been previously canceled. Thus, Claims 1, 3, 4, 6, and 7 are presently pending, with Claims 1, 6, and 7 being independent.
Applicant respectfully requests reconsideration and allowance of the claims in view of the presented amendments and accompanying remarks. Statement of Substance of Interview

On January 29, 2025, Applicant's undersigned representative held a telephonic interview with Examiner Alqaderi and Examiner Liang. Applicant and Applicant's representative appreciate the Examiners' willingness to conduct and courtesies extended during the telephonic interview. Applicant submits this summary to record Applicant's representative's understanding of the substance of the interview. To the extent Applicant's understanding is incorrect, notice of such would be appreciated.

On the call, the parties discussed the rejection of Claim 1 under Section 103 and possible amendments for advancing prosecution. The Examiners agreed that amendments generally consistent with the amendments made to the claims in this submission would overcome the current rejections. Thus Applicant has amended independent Claims 1, 6, and 7 in a manner consistent with the suggestions made during the interview.
It is respectfully submitted that the instant STATEMENT OF SUBSTANCE OF INTERVIEW complies with the requirements of 37 C.F.R. @@ 1.2 and 1.133 and M.P.E.P. @ 713.04.
Claims 1, 3, 4, 6, and 7 are rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 103 as purportedly being
unpatentable over Takae (US 2018/0222422), in view of Watanabe (US 2018/0105185), Aoki (US
Applicant respectfully traverses these rejections for at least the following reasons and
discusses independent Claim 1 as an example.
Without any admissions, independent Claim 1 has been amended to recite:
A vehicle control device configured to control a vehicle, comprising:
an information provision device configured to provide information to a
driver of the vehicle;

a processor, during automated driving control of the vehicle, configured to: perform the automated driving control by automatically performing a driving operation of the vehicle relating to an automated driving plan of the vehicle control device, the automated driving control comprising operations relating to at least one of acceleration, steering, and braking,
according to the automated driving plan;
provide, through the information provision device to the driver, a driving event that is to occur at a subsequent point ahead in a direction of
advance from a current point, based on the automated driving plan;

judge whether a driver driving operation being performed by the driver at the current point before the subsequent point of the driving event is acceptable to be performed, the driving event being a lane change to a first lane at a first side of the vehicle, the driver driving operation being a lane change to a second lane at the first side of the vehicle performed at the current point before the subsequent point of the driving event, the judging being based on whether the second lane is unable to be driven on between the current point and the subsequent point of the driving event due to at least
one of a blockage or an ending of the second lane;

provide, through the information provision device to the driver, judgment information that causes the driver not to perform the driver driving operation, based on the judging that the driver driving operation is unacceptable according to the automated driving plan being executed by the vehicle control device, the judgment information comprising lane change inhibiting information indicating that the second lane is unable to be driven on between the current point and the subsequent point of the driving event due to the at least one of the blockage or the ending of the second lane; and

provide, through the information provision device to the driver together with the judgment information, distance information from the current point to a point where the second lane is unable to be driven due to the at least one of the blockage or the ending of the second lane.

At a minimum, the proposed Takae-Watanabe-Aoki-Masui combination does not disclose or suggest to "provide, through the information provision device to the driver together with the judgment information, distance information from the current point to a point where the second lane is unable to be driven due to the at least one of the blockage or the ending of the second lane", as recited in Claim 1.

The Office Action acknowledges that Takae and Watanabe do not disclose the cited features of Claim 1. See Office Action, p. 8. Instead, the Office Action relies on Aoki and Masui as allegedly disclosing these features. Applicant respectfully submits that Aoki and Masui do not make up for at least the above-discussed deficiencies of Takae and Watanabe.

Aoki is generally directed to a driver performing a steering intervention while "a vehicle is traveling by autonomous driving control". See Aoki, [0006]. In particular, Aoki discloses a control device that determines "whether there arises an excessive approach to an obstacle that is present on a lane to which the vehicle intends to move based on a relative distance from the obstacle, during execution of the autonomous lane change control". See id. at [0018]. According to Aoki, "it can be determined that the stop condition of autonomous lane change is established, when the vehicle excessively approaches an obstacle on the lane to which the vehicle intends to move during execution of the autonomous lane change control", such that "when the driver forces lane change under the situation in which such an excessive approach occurs, termination of the autonomous driving control can be announced appropriately." See id. at [0033].

That is, at best, Aoki discloses determining whether there is an obstacle present on a lane to which the vehicle intends to move and announcing termination of autonomous driving control when the driver forces a lane change.

To the extent the Office is attempting to equate the determining of whether there is an obstacle present of Aoki to the claimed "judgement information", Claim 1 recites to "provide, through the information provision device to the driver together with the judgment information [that causes the driver not to perform the driver driving operation], distance information from the current point to a point where the second lane is unable to be driven due to the at least one of the blockage or the ending of the second lane." Aoki does not disclose providing any such information to the driver. Indeed, at best, Aoki discloses announcing termination of autonomous driving control when the driver forces a lane change.
Consequently, Aoki is unable to disclose or suggest at least the cited features recited in Claim 1.

Masui does not make up for at least the above-discussed deficiencies of Takae, Watanabe, and Aoki. Masui generally directed to a cruise control apparatus with a course prediction section that includes an other vehicle's trajectory acquisition unit. See Masui, FIG. 1 and [0022]. According to Masui, based "on the distance measurement data (information on distance and lateral position in relation to the own vehicle and the preceding vehicle) from the radar device 12, the other vehicle's trajectory acquisition unit 25 cyclically calculates the preceding-vehicle positions, consisting of coordinates expressing points traversed by a preceding vehicle, and stores the calculated preceding-vehicle positions in chronological order." Id. at [0024]. Masui further discloses that the other vehicle's trajectory acquisition unit "calculates path information for not only a vehicle traveling in the same lane as the own vehicle but also a vehicle traveling in a lane
adjacent to that of the own vehicle, from among the preceding vehicles, and uses the information in predicting the course of the own vehicle". Id.

That is, at best, Masui discloses predicting the course of an own vehicle based on path information for a vehicle traveling in the same lane as the own vehicle and a vehicle traveling in a lane adjacent to that of the own vehicle that has been calculated using distance measurement data.

Nowhere, however, does Masui disclose or suggest to "provide, through the information provision device to the driver together with the judgment information [that causes the driver not to perform the driver driving operation], distance information from the current point to a point where the second lane is unable to be driven due to the at least one of the blockage or the ending of the second lane", as recited in Claim 1.
Consequently, Masui is unable to disclose or suggest at least the cited features recited in Claim 1.

Thus, even assuming for the sake of argument only that the proposed Takae-Watanabe- Aoki-Masui combination would have been proper, which Applicant does not concede, the proposed combination does not disclose, teach, or suggest all features recited in Claim 1.
In view of the above, Applicant respectfully submits that Claim 1 is patentable over the cited references and requests withdrawal of the rejection.

To the extent that independent Claims 6 and 7 recite features similar to the above-noted features of Claim 1, Applicant submits that Claims 6 and 7 are patentable for at least reasons similar to those discussed above with respect to Claim 1.

Applicant respectfully submits that dependent Claims 3 and 4 are patentable due to their respective dependencies, as well as for their additional features. This should not be construed as an acquiescence to Examiner's interpretation of the claims, or reading of those claim elements on
the prior art, and Applicant expressly reserves the right to establish the patentability of those additional claim limitations, should the need arise. Conclusion

In view of the above, reconsideration and allowance of this application are now believed to be in order, and such actions are hereby solicited.
